Properties.Composition.why: the properties are stated against the composition's own functions and the core interface's, on Lean core: nothing of Mathlib or of `security`

Properties.Pouw.why: the properties are stated against the code's own functions, on Lean core: nothing of Mathlib or of `security`

Properties.Pouw.Commit.why: the commitments' properties are stated against the port's own functions, on Lean core: nothing of Mathlib or of `security`

Properties.Nci.why: a property is stated over the definitions and the code it is about, never over a proof

Properties.NciDesc.why: the description-sized check's properties are stated over the code they are about (NciCheck.Desc, and NciCheck.Baseline, the check of record), the NCI properties they relate it to, and the named assumptions a verdict's bounds rest on (Definitions.Nci.Assumptions), never over a proof

Properties.CertifierDevice.why: the properties are stated against the device's own step and issuer, on Lean core: nothing of Mathlib or of `security`

Properties.Pous.why: a property is stated over the definitions and the code it is about, never over a proof

Properties.Identity.why: the bridge is stated against core's identity hash and C-Flock's SHA-512, on Lean core: nothing of Mathlib or of `security`

Properties.NetworkCertifier.why: the properties are stated against the code's own functions, the check's and N2's link-window verdict of record's, and the certificates the certifier's device signs against LMS's own signer (`CertifierSigned`), never a proof

Properties.Evaluate.why: the evaluator's equalities are stated against its functions and the `Definitions.Core` modules they copy, which import nothing of Mathlib

Properties.NetworkRecords.why: what the records check's acceptance means is stated against its own functions and the reference Program's grid, with v2's statements of the evidence, the syncs and the heads, never a proof

Properties.SampledProofs.why: the properties are stated against the one-stage audit's own functions, on Lean core: nothing of Mathlib or of `security`

Properties.CertifierNetwork.why: the guarantees join the device's statements and the check's, with the network lane's premise (`Definitions.NetworkCertifier.Premises`) and the reference Program they are read against: stated over their definitions, never a proof

Properties.RemoteAudit.why: the properties are stated against the verifier's own functions, on Lean core: nothing of Mathlib or of `security`

Properties.Accounting.why: the requirement code's equalities are stated against its functions and the `Definitions.Accounting.Requirement` definitions they copy, never a proof

Properties.SampledProofs.Draw.why: what the draw misses is stated against `Select.select`'s slots (`SampledProofs.Slots`) and the claims' miss probability `P_a` (`Definitions.Claims`), never a proof

Properties.Accounting.Compose.why: a declared circuit's proof units, commit coins and draw (`Definitions.Accounting.Compose`) are stated against the verifier's own partition of its program (`SampledProofs.Slots.layout`) and the challenger's draw from bytes (`SampledProofs.Select.select`, read as `Properties.SampledProofs.bytesOf` reads them), never a proof

Properties.Accounting.Served.why: the served window's units and draw (`Definitions.Accounting.Served`) are stated against each call's Program's partition (`SampledProofs.Slots.layout`, `SampledProofs.Partition.units`) and the verifier's population draw (`SampledProofs.Draw.drawUnits`, from bytes as `Properties.SampledProofs.bytesOf` reads them), beside `Properties.Compose.UnitsOfLayout`, never a proof

Properties.Pouw.Credit.why: the ε a credit reports is stated against the code's strata, law and epsAt (`Properties.Pouw.Strata`, on Lean core), its draw as `Properties.SampledProofs.bytesOf` reads uniform streams and its probability `Pouw.RelativeSecurity.prob` (`Definitions.Pouw.RelativeSecurity`), never a proof

Properties.RemoteAudit.Pooled.why: the pooled bound the verifier computes (`RemoteAudit.Pooled`) and the W the memory line reads (`RemoteAudit.Line`) are stated against the draw's model they cover (`Definitions.Accounting.Remote.Draw`), never a proof

Properties.RemoteAudit.Line.why: the memory line of record is stated against the line's and the verifier's own functions (RemoteAudit) and the memory model's trace, paced session, draw and premises (Definitions.Accounting.Remote, Definitions.Accounting.Assumptions), its probability `Pouw.pr` (Definitions.Pouw.Basic); never a proof

Properties.RemoteAudit.Schedule.why: the schedule check (`RemoteAudit.Schedule`) is stated against the code, and the gap it leaves against the layout vocabulary it feeds (`Definitions.Accounting.Schedule`), never a proof

Properties.Pous.Period.why: a period's PoUS audit is stated over the deployed check it is about and the joint run of the device model (`Definitions.Accounting`) whose capacity audit it is, never over a proof

Properties.Verity.why: soundness at the verifier of record is stated over onsite's compiled code and its SHA-512, the composition's properties, the committed files as the verifier reads them (Flock.Bridge.circuitOfFile), the period model's vocabulary (Accounting.PeriodLive, the one definition of a period), the shared game and the row-leaf opening it reads the commitment through, never over a proof

Properties.Pouw.Period.why: the period's work at the deployed check's accepted prefix is stated against the check's own verdict (`PouwCheck.protocol.check`) and the accounting model's period, its proofs and its named claims (`Definitions.Accounting.ComposePeriod`, `Definitions.Accounting.Assumptions`), never a proof

Properties.Accounting.JointBridge.WorkOf.why: a joint period's audit bridge is stated over the joint period (`Definitions.Accounting.JointPeriod`), the bridge's realization and the H200's price (`Definitions.Accounting.JointBridge`), its named premises (`Definitions.Accounting.Assumptions.CreditedWords`) and the source protocol's period statement (`Properties.Pouw.Period`), never a proof

Properties.Accounting.DeclaredCircuit.why: the declared circuit's requirement at the committed steering cap is stated over the memory model's game and premises (`Definitions.Accounting`, `Accounting.Guarantees.DeclaredCircuitRequirement`'s module) and the schedule check's statements and gap (`Properties.RemoteAudit.Schedule`), never a proof

Properties.Flock.why: the circuit a parsed C-Flock circuit file is built into (`Placed.keyProg`, `Layout.outsOf`, `Built`) is defined over the verifier's own types and checks (`Flock.Circuit`, `Flock.Net`) and C-Flock's circuit vocabulary (`Definitions.Flock.Circuit`), and is core's circuit and partition (`Definitions.Core`) at the parsed and the committed file (`Flock.Bridge.circuitOf`, `circuitOfFile`), never a proof

Properties.Accounting.JointBridge.why: a protocol's per-period guarantee read as the coins model's (`PeriodRun.Sound`) is stated over the period (`Definitions.Accounting.JointPeriod`), its bridge (`Definitions.Accounting.JointBridge`), the bridge's named claims (`Definitions.Accounting.Assumptions`) and the protocol's own period statement (`Properties.Pous.Period`, `Properties.Pouw.Period`), never a proof

Properties.Accounting.JointBridge.WorkOf.why: a joint period's PoUW bridge from a credit in words is stated over the joint period (`Definitions.Accounting.JointPeriod`), its realization (`Definitions.Accounting.JointBridge.CreditedWords`) and its named premises (`Definitions.Accounting.Assumptions.CreditedWords`), never a proof or a source protocol's statement

Properties.Pouw.PeriodJ10R.why: the period's credit at served H1's accepted prefix is stated against its own verdict (`PouwCheck.Credit.window`) and draw (`Credit.drawnOf`), the accounting model's period and J10-R's noise (`Definitions.Accounting.ComposePeriod`, `Definitions.Accounting.TS.J10R`), its named claims and `Properties.Pouw.Period`'s salt premise, never a proof

Properties.NetworkPeriod.why: what the period check's rows-form K counts is stated against its own terms (`rowsTerms`) and Mathlib's finite products, never a proof

Properties.RemoteAudit.Component.why: the bandwidth component's refinement is stated against its own check (`RemoteAudit.Protocol`) and the memory line of record (`Properties.RemoteAudit.Line`), whose model vocabulary it reads through that module; never a proof

Properties.Pouw.ServedValues.why: the served period's values in AND gates are stated against served H1's period and premises (`Properties.Pouw.PeriodJ10R`) and the AND count (`Definitions.Core.Formalism`), never a proof

Properties.Attest.why: a party's signed periods are stated over the code that checks them (MemoryChallenger.Attest, Lms.Hss), the memory challenger's string framing, the claims' collision finders (Claims.Finder) and the party assumptions (Accounting.Assumptions.Parties), never over a proof

frozen.Pous.Period.SecurityProofs.periodHeldDep: frozen (premise): periodHeld at the deployed ring budget (RING_D, RING_Q, RING_L) = (16,446, 2^20, 2^64), the one pous-ring-speed derives from Delta + RTT = 854,000 ns and the measured round floor ROUND_NS = 361.55 / 3.490 ns (art:23a323f3, r20260929-060834-0ec4): DEADLINE_ROUNDS = 8,243 <= RING_D, and RING_D + 1 rounds take 1.995 x the limit; outside both regions where P2RingAuditSecure is refuted (D >= 32,894; L >= 2^169 at k = 105). frozen.Pous.Period.SecurityProofs.periodHeldHon: completeness: the honest lemma of periodHeld and periodHeldDeployed: at an honest period on one H200 holding all of C* (honestRun, 2^30 bits on chip, one PCIe Gen 5 x16 side channel of 437,248,000 bits a round), RingDevice holds at the deployed budget for every audit, the certificate HONEST_S = 63,000,000 bits is positive and fits the state bound, and the budget is the deadline's at the measured floor (DEADLINE_ROUNDS <= RING_D, the 1.995x margin)
frozen.Pous.Period.SecurityProofs.periodHeldNon: completeness: the nontrivial lemma of periodHeld and periodHeldDeployed: at a period whose capacity account holds nothing, an accept-all verdict fails their conclusion wherever the period's data holds no break (a concrete audit with no break needs SHA-512 on each of the table's 2^20 strings, so that is a hypothesis), and their event is false at the honest period
frozen.Properties.Pouw.ServedValues.SecurityPro: frozen (no-function,world-unlisted): H1J10RCheckedCreditPeriod's period and premises, less UnitFixed and the play's folded words, with its bound in AND gates of the registered declaration D under the lowering pinned at registration (Verity.creditSize, Definitions.Core.Formalism): except with probability delta_s + n(delta_bind + delta_ks), delta_coin plus delta_crypto, an accepted period's right blocks (DrawnLayer.Good under periodMode) have total AND count at least (1 - eps_skip)_+ S, S the credited size of the windows before the first refusal, eps_skip = sigma eps(j) N_live / S, and each block's AND count taken outside the ledger of gates another protocol credits; not one acceptance hypothesis, a Pouw.RelativeSecurity.prob event that shape.events does not list. A values guarantee, not a compute claim: right values aren't work. Right is the accounting model's DrawnLayer.Good, not yet tied to the committed values Credit.window checks. No premise beyond H1's: TileDrawIsCoin, TileServiceSound, RegisteredBeforeDraw, SaltIsLiveCoin and SharedNoiseLucks, the one computational premise. Proved from H1J10RCheckedCreditPeriod at a play whose fixed words are the right blocks' (Proofs.Pouw.ServedValues), with an honest and a nontrivial witness (Proofs.Pouw.ServedValues.Honest).

Pous.P2.Assumptions.P2RingAuditSecure.why: P2 in the ring model at the deployed point accepts a rho-bounded, (D, Q, L)-bounded responder with probability at most 1% + 2^-129 + 2^-130; open, and, if p is prime, false at D >= 32,894 (Q >= 2, L >= 65,789) for every k (PousP2Ring.tight_p16448, Security/Proofs/Pous/P2/RingTight.lean), and at L >= 2^30 for k <= 88 (PousP2Ring.not_meetsOn_b19_k88, Security/Proofs/Pous/P2/RingTrunc.lean); and, at k = 105, from L >= 2^169 with D >= 2 and Q >= 2 (Pous.Period.SecurityProofs.not_p2RingAuditSecure_trunc, Security/Proofs/Pous/PeriodDeployed.lean: 501,819 blocks without their low 168 bits), so the deployed budget (16,446, 2^20, 2^64) lies outside every refuted region. Its test plays the ring-model audit at a scaled point (w = 184, 16 blocks, lambda = 9) with those two attacks and seeded bounded responders.
